articles.detail: 5 cycles, 5 completed, avg 11.8/cycle; selections were 11/10/13/15/12 against targets of 11/12/13/15/15; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active and no pause gate is set. Every goal is met except Latin America datelines (3% against 5%), which is one day's reading after 8% yesterday; the one lever for it, GAP_COUNTRIES, was tried and reverted on 2026-09-23 with Mexico and Argentina producing no datelines, so a single low day does not justify repeating it.
weakestArea: Latin America is 2 of 59 datelines (Uruapan and Brasília), 3% against a 5% target, down from 8% on Sunday when the Brazilian first round carried it. Tech recovered to 13 for the day but was still under its per-cycle floor after dedup in three of five cycles (2, 1 and 2 against 3), and science reached its target of 5 with one pick or none in four cycles, so both remain supply-bound rather than healthy.
watching: Brazil: Flávio Bolsonaro leads after the first round, with a runoff against Lula to come.
Spain: Sánchez called a snap election after his minority government lost votes in Congress.
Hormuz: Qatari liquefied natural gas crossed the strait, Middle East crude exports rose above pre-war levels, and Aramco warned of a two-year shortage.
Yemen: the government claims gains at Dhubab while the Houthis warn Saudi Arabia over its airspace and Washington backs Riyadh's right to defend itself.
Ethiopia: federal forces retook Mekelle and an interim administration for Tigray is being prepared.
Pakistan: talks with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf collapsed as petrol prices rose and a sixth polio case was confirmed.
Russia: US secondary sanctions on its trade partners are due on 18 October, and the Kremlin would not comment on a reported oil deal.
Irkutsk: a plague institute worker died; the region's account of the health situation is sourced to state media alone.
ASML's 8.6% share move was flagged by the selector again with no story in the feed to explain it.
coverageGaps: Latin America had two datelines all day, one of them the Brazilian election follow-up.
Oceania had no dateline; the sixth region counted is a single global-tagged story.
Tech was under its floor after dedup in the 05:00, 10:00 and 22:00 cycles, when the feed carried no Hacker News, Ars Technica, 404 Media, Decoder or Register items.
Science was under its floor in four of five cycles and published nothing at 22:00; the 10:00 cycle's only real science story was the Nobel.
Economy had no multi-source pick in the 10:00 cycle, and two of its picks there were thin Bloomberg teasers.
Thin picks were recovered for 6 of 11 sources across the day, and for 0 of 2 at 10:00.
Five articles are sourced only from state or advocacy outlets, down from 11 yesterday: three on Iran, one on Irkutsk and one on US firms in Ukraine.
Freshness was measured on 2 of 59 articles, so the median of 0 is indicative only.
context: A normal Monday after a thin weekend: all five cycles completed in an average of 886s (selector 199s, writer 194s, editor 103s) and the selector met its target in three cycles and fell short by 2 and 3 in the others. Science plus tech returned to 31% from 15%, with Nature, Dialogue Earth and Ars Technica back among the science sources, so yesterday's shortfall was the weekend feed and the CURATED_SOURCES experiment floated in that audit is not needed yet. Odds rows were offered in four cycles (9 rows) and two articles cite Polymarket, both on Yemen and Saudi Arabia, in line with the rule kept on 2026-10-04.
